rationale: Stem asks for the most likely effect of the Navigation Acts on Atlantic port cities; the student must explain the effects of a historical policy (concentrating colonial exports/English imports in ports, enriching merchants). That is explaining a historical development/process -> 1.B. Content is colonial Atlantic trade restrictions -> topic 2.4 Transatlantic Trade (unit 2 matches period U2).

Stem asks which relationship between two developments (steel technology via the Bessemer process and industrial business demand) the Eads Bridge best illustrates; the key explains the feedback loop between them. That is explaining how one historical development relates to another -> 5.B (Making Connections). Content is 1870s steel technology enabling giant projects -> topic 6.5 Technological Innovation (unit 6 matches U6).

Stem asks how the typewriter (like the telephone) changed business; the key explains the mechanism (made corporate-scale paperwork and communication feasible). That is explaining a historical development/process -> 1.B. Content is business communication technology of the 1880s-1890s -> topic 6.5 Technological Innovation (unit 6 matches U6).

Stem asks why electric streetcars helped create 'streetcar suburbs'; the key explains the causal mechanism (allowed living farther from work, separating home and workplace, enabling middle-class suburban homeownership). That is explaining a historical development/process -> 1.B. Content is middle-class suburbanization -> topic 6.10 Development of the Middle Class (unit 6 matches U6).

Stem asks what the department store represented compared with the small general store; the key identifies it as retail organized on the era's large industrial scale. The task is identification/characterization of a development, not explaining a causal mechanism -> 1.A. Content is mass consumer retail serving the new middle class -> topic 6.10 Development of the Middle Class (unit 6 matches U6).

Stem presents an 1867 sharecropping contract as a primary source and asks what it is most valuable for showing; the key answers with the source's evidentiary use (the legal terms binding tenants to landowners). That is explaining the use(s) of a source, not its POV or audience -> 2.C. Content is post-emancipation Southern labor systems -> topic 6.4 The 'New South' (unit 6 matches U6).

Stem asks for the definition of 'majority-minority' in the context of immigration-driven demographic change; constrained to the item's skill field (Contextualization), the closest sub-code is 4.A (identify and describe a historical context - here the demographic context). HOWEVER: the content is really a vocabulary identification item -> 1.A material; skill field likely mislabeled. Topic is immigration-driven demographic change -> 9.5 Migration and Immigration in the 1990s and 2000s (unit 9 matches U9).

Stem asks which combination of push and pull factors best explains large Latin American immigration in the 1980s-2000s; the key explains the causation (U.S. jobs/family ties as pull, poverty/instability as push). That is explaining a historical development/process -> 1.B. Topic is immigration 1980s-2000s -> 9.5 Migration and Immigration in the 1990s and 2000s (unit 9 matches U9).

Stem presents Reagan's 1983 'evil empire' language and asks what shift it signaled from the detente era; the key identifies the speech's purpose/POV (a return to moral confrontation after negotiated coexistence). Constrained to Sourcing & Situation, identifying a source's purpose/point of view -> 2.A. HOWEVER: the item really tests knowledge of the foreign-policy shift itself, so the skill field is arguably Developments & Processes. Topic is Reagan's Cold War turn -> 9.2 Reagan and Conservatism (unit 9 matches U9).

Stem uses the 1980-1985 military-spending chart to ask how Reagan's approach differed from Nixon's detente; the key explains Reagan's buildup as situated within (and departing from) the broader Cold War context of detente-era coexistence. Constrained to Contextualization -> 4.B. HOWEVER: the item is fundamentally a comparison (reasoning field is Comparison), so 5.A/5.B territory; skill field questionable. Topic is Reagan's foreign policy -> 9.2 Reagan and Conservatism (unit 9 matches U9).

Stem uses the mid-1980s oil-price collapse chart to ask what systemic difference explains why the U.S. weathered it while the USSR was devastated; the key explains the mechanism (flexible market economy reallocated; rigid command economy dependent on oil exports). That is explaining a historical development/process -> 1.B. Content is the Soviet economic collapse at the Cold War's end -> 9.3 The End of the Cold War (unit 9 matches U9).

Stem uses the 2000-2010 military-spending chart to ask which sequence of events drove the increase; the key identifies the two ground wars in order (Afghanistan 2001, then Iraq 2003). The task is identifying the historical developments, not explaining their mechanism -> 1.A. Topic is the War on Terror -> 9.6 Challenges of the 21st Century (unit 9 matches U9).

Stem uses the post-2006 home-price collapse chart and asks what the 2009-2010 Tea Party movement was primarily a reaction against; the key explains how the movement relates to the crisis-era interventions (bailouts, stimulus, ACA seen as overreach). That is explaining how one development relates to another -> 5.B (Making Connections). Topic is 2008-crisis fallout politics -> 9.6 Challenges of the 21st Century (unit 9 matches U9).

Stem uses the 1992-2000 deficit-to-surplus chart and asks what Clinton's triangulation ('era of big government is over', 1996 welfare reform) shows about the era's political climate; the key explains his approach as situated within a broader context where limited-government ideas dominated even a Democratic presidency. That is explaining how a development is situated within a broader historical context -> 4.B. Topic is the Reagan revolution's lasting political legacy -> 9.2 Reagan and Conservatism (unit 9 matches U9).

Stem uses the chart's 1986 deficit figure ($221B, five years after the 1981 tax cuts) to ask what it shows about supply-side theory's central prediction; the key states the evidence refutes the claim (deficits tripled instead of the cuts paying for themselves). That is explaining how evidence refutes an argument -> 3.D. Topic is the 1981 tax cuts and their deficit consequences -> 9.2 Reagan and Conservatism (unit 9 matches U9).
